raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

NIXL EP sizes every dispatch with the static `max_tokens_per_rank` reservation (typically `max_num_batched_tokens`, e.g. 8192), so expert workspaces, zeroing and grouped-GEMM grids scale with 8192 rows even when a decode step has a few dozen tokens per rank. This PR passes the synchronized DP/SP execution size instead and keeps the static value as the reservation bound. DeepEP v2 already does the same (`deepep_v2.py`, `num_max_tokens_per_rank` bounded by `max(num_tokens_across_dp)`).

Related: #61156 takes a different approach to the same cost by lowering the static NIXL bound to 1024 with synchronized chunking. The two can combine; I'll coordinate there.

## Claims

- NIXL dispatch capacity = max synchronized execution tokens across DP ranks (EP-local SP sizes when sequence parallelism is active), aligned to NIXL's receive extent (a multiple of 4 across dispatchers), and bounded by `max_tokens_per_rank`. The capacity is identical on every rank because it comes from the same CPU DP metadata, including during CUDA graph capture.
- The NIXL buffer reservation is unchanged.
- For `BatchedExperts`, the fused output is a contiguous `[E, M, K]` view of the runtime dispatch shape, while the workspace keeps its static reservation.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.
- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k nixl_ep` on 2x H200 (DP2/EP2, real NIXL dispatch/combine checked against the reference MoE): 52/52 subcases pass before and after (BF16, FP8 blocked, ModelOpt FP8; `m=222` against a 256-token reservation, so both the runtime capacity and the `BatchedExperts` view are exercised). This used main's test files on the `77154ca611` base described below.

Historical A/B on an older snapshot (2026-09-20/21, H200, DP8/EP8, DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16, NIXL EP, `batched_triton`, rank loads `[63,97,80,80,80,80,80,80]`, FULL graph bucket 128). The two runs' source patches differ only by this change. They were measured under Nsight, so the numbers are per-step kernel timings, not serving throughput.

| per decode step (rank average) | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| dispatch capacity, DBO off | 8192 | 128 |
| dispatch capacity, DBO on | 8192 | 64 + 64 |
| workspace zero, DBO off | 11.299 ms | 0.205 ms |
| workspace zero, DBO on | 22.607 ms | 0.254 ms |
| step wall, DBO off | 35.467 ms | 23.555 ms |

End-to-end A/B, no profiler. Before is main@`77154ca611`, the last commit with a cu129 precompiled wheel, which matches this host's driver. After is the same commit with this change cherry-picked. The `nixl_ep.py` code path is unchanged on main since then. Setup: 2x H200, DP2/EP2, DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16, NIXL EP, `batched_triton`, FULL CUDA graphs, DBO off.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend nixl_ep --moe-backend batched_triton --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA \
  --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --seed 0 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL"}'
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256 \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 128 --ignore-eos --seed 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0
```

| metric (2 rounds each, after a warmup) | before | after | change |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| output throughput (tok/s) | 2082.6 / 2097.8 | 2647.1 / 2673.6 | **+27.3%** |
| mean TPOT (ms) | 58.68 / 58.76 | 45.57 / 45.13 | **−22.8%** |
| mean TTFT (ms) | 744.6 / 616.8 | 737.7 / 726.5 | ~same |
| GSM8K accuracy (1319 q, 5-shot, greedy), 3 runs | 0.3525 / 0.3503 / 0.3457 | 0.3427 / 0.3480 / 0.3480 | mean 0.3495 → 0.3462 |

All requests succeeded. GSM8K runs 2 and 3 come from a second server launch per side. The mean difference (−0.33 pt, about 4 of 1319 questions) is within the before side's own run-to-run spread (0.68 pt), so I read it as noise: vLLM is not batch invariant, and the smaller expert `M` can select a different batched-Triton tile configuration.

## Details

- `_get_runtime_dispatch_capacity()` reads `dp_metadata.local_sizes` (set by `sp_local_sizes()` under SP) or `num_tokens_across_dp_cpu`. Both are CPU values, so there is no GPU sync.
- The alignment only affects undersized warmup shapes. With 8 dispatchers it is a no-op.
- The `modular_kernel.py` change applies to every `BatchedExperts` backend. For batched experts `M_full` is `a1q.size(1)`, the dispatched row count. DeepEP low-latency and the naive batched prepare/finalize still dispatch with their static capacity, so `M_full` equals the old `fused_out_shape[1]` and the view is unchanged for them. The workspace reservation still uses the static shape.
- CI: the H100 FusedMoE layer step has no nixl installed, so `has_nixl_ep()` skips every `nixl_ep` case in `test_moe_layer.py`. The second commit installs the KV connector dependencies in that step, as the fault tolerance step does, so these cases run in CI. Locally the `nixl_ep` cases add about 3 minutes.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

files.patch:
@@ -911,6 +911,8 @@ steps:
   - vllm/distributed/device_communicators/
   - vllm/config
   commands:
+    # Base image has no nixl; install it or has_nixl_ep() skips the nixl_ep cases.
+    - bash /vllm-workspace/.buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh
     - pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py
   mirror:
     amd:

@@ -1164,6 +1164,12 @@ def _allocate_buffers(
         # process-wide high-water mark; later graph shapes may need this
         # storage for workspace13.
         max_shape_size = max(prod(workspace13_shape), prod(fused_out_shape))
+        if (
+            self.fused_experts.activation_format()
+            == FusedMoEActivationFormat.BatchedExperts
+        ):
+            assert M_full <= fused_out_shape[1]
+            fused_out_shape = (fused_out_shape[0], M_full, fused_out_shape[2])
 
         if current_platform.is_cpu():
             # Every CPU FusedMoEExpertsModular kernel reports zero-sized

@@ -1,11 +1,13 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 from collections.abc import Callable
+from math import gcd
 
 import nixl_ep
 import torch
 
 import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.modular_kernel as mk
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context, is_forward_context_available
 from vllm.logger import init_logger
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import FusedMoEQuantConfig
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.topk_weight_and_reduce import (
@@ -137,6 +139,28 @@ def activation_format(self) -> mk.FusedMoEActivationFormat:
     def max_num_tokens_per_rank(self) -> int | None:
         return self.max_tokens_per_rank
 
+    def _get_runtime_dispatch_capacity(self) -> int:
+        """Use the synchronized execution slice, retaining the reservation limit."""
+        if not is_forward_context_available():
+            return self.max_tokens_per_rank
+        dp_metadata = get_forward_context().dp_metadata
+        if dp_metadata is None:
+            return self.max_tokens_per_rank
+        # The MoE runner supplies EP-local sizes when sequence parallelism is
+        # active. Both sources are CPU metadata, including during graph capture.
+        if dp_metadata.local_sizes is not None:
+            capacity = max(dp_metadata.local_sizes)
+        else:
+            capacity = int(dp_metadata.num_tokens_across_dp_cpu.max())
+        capacity = max(1, capacity)
+        # The NIXL TMA receive extent is capacity * num_dispatchers and must
+        # be divisible by four. This only changes undersized warmup shapes;
+        # normal aligned execution buckets (for example 64/128) are unchanged.
+        alignment = 4 // gcd(self.num_dispatchers_, 4)
+        capacity = (capacity + alignment - 1) // alignment * alignment
+        assert capacity <= self.max_tokens_per_rank
+        return capacity
+
     def topk_indices_dtype(self) -> torch.dtype | None:
         return NIXL_EP_TOPK_INDICES_DTYPE
 
@@ -247,11 +271,13 @@ def prepare_async(
             a1 = a1 * topk_weights.to(a1.dtype)
 
         # Dispatch
+        runtime_dispatch_capacity = self._get_runtime_dispatch_capacity()
+        assert a1.size(0) <= runtime_dispatch_capacity
         dispatch_topk_ids = self._map_global_to_physical_ids(topk_ids)
         expert_x, expert_num_tokens, handle, _, hook = self.buffer.dispatch(
             a1,
             dispatch_topk_ids,
-            self.max_tokens_per_rank,
+            runtime_dispatch_capacity,
             self.expert_capacity,
             use_fp8=self.use_fp8_dispatch,
             # round_scale needs to be set to dispatch in ue8m0
